title: Asynchronous AI Engineer Hire Lab + Remote Bootcamp (30d)
body:
Purpose:
This doc defines a repeatable, lightweight asynchronous hiring experiment for mid-senior ML / inference engineers that pairs a short, take-home lab with a structured 30-day remote bootcamp to accelerate ramp and validate product fit before full offer commitments. The goal is to reduce time-to-hire, improve signal for remote candidates, and provide a candidate experience that mirrors day-to-day work (async collaboration + short pairing).

When to use:
- Hiring for roles where distributed autonomy and asynchronous communication are primary success signals (inference, infra, platform).
- When travel/onsite loops are undesirable or time-constrained.
- For senior ICs and staff-level hires where system design + execution matters more than whiteboard speed.

Stakeholders / Owners:
- People Ops (owner): Jordan Patel
- Hiring manager: (role-specific)
- Interview panel lead: senior eng on team (recommended: 2 panelists)
- Onboarding partner: People Ops onboarding SME (Maya Chen)

High-level flow (candidate-facing):
1) Recruiter screens for baseline fit and logistics (timezones, tooling).
2) Candidate receives Async Hire Kit (48–72h suggested turnaround).
3) Candidate submits lab + short video walkthrough (10–12 minutes) and fills short context form.
4) Panel asynchronously scores using the rubric below within 3 business days.
5) If pass -> invite to 30d paid bootcamp contract (2–4 weeks paid contractor contract, optionally convertible to full-time).
6) Bootcamp: week-by-week deliverables, weekly syncs, and a final stakeholder demo.
7) Final hiring decision and offer discussion.

Async Hire Kit (what we send):
- A two-part assignment: (A) small systems design + tradeoff brief (1–2 pages), (B) implementation sketch + pseudo-code or runnable notebook solving a constrained inference problem (core: latency/cost tradeoffs).
- Starter repo (skeleton), sample dataset subset, and docker/colab run instructions.
- Clear acceptance criteria and scoring rubric summary.
- Optional: 10–12min screen-recorded walkthrough where candidate explains assumptions and key choices.
- Time expectation: 8–12 hours of focused work (explicitly stated).

Sample Async Tasks:
1) Throughput optimization micro-task: Given a toy model and traces, propose and simulate a batching strategy to respect a 50ms P50 latency SLO at X qps. Provide numeric estimates and a short script that demonstrates the plan on the sample traces.
2) Fallback routing policy brief: Design a simple routing/fallback policy when a high-cost model is temporarily unavailable. Include a short pseudo-PR that modifies a route config and rationale for metrics to track.
3) Debug & triage snippet: Small failing notebook / inference pipeline step; candidate identifies root cause, suggests fix, and lists 3 mitigation steps to prevent recurrence in prod.

Scoring rubric (panel uses same sheet; each criterion 1–5, notes required):
- Systems thinking (1–5): clarity of tradeoffs, awareness of production constraints (latency/cost/reliability).
- Execution plan (1–5): feasibility, clearness of next steps, testability of proposal.
- Code & reproducibility (1–5): code quality, ability to run with provided artifacts, documentation.
- Communication & async clarity (1–5): brevity and clarity in written/video explanation; assumptions explicit.
- Product impact & prioritization (1–5): sense of impact relative to user problems and business levers.
Pass thresholds (recommended): average >= 3.8 across categories, no score <=2 in a critical criterion (systems thinking or execution). Panel may escalate to hiring manager for borderline cases.

Candidate Experience Notes (must include in message):
- We pay a flat stipend for the async lab completion (recommended USD 400–800 depending on role) to reduce selection bias and encourage completion.
- Provide clear runbook: how to run the sample job, expected runtime, and what to submit.
- Explicitly state whether the assignment is normative (we evaluate process and explanation) vs. product code we might later use (we will not reuse candidate IP without consent).

30-day Paid Bootcamp (objective + structure):
- Objective: validate productive collaboration, technical execution speed, and cultural fit on a real, scoped ticket that delivers measurable infra/product impact.
- Commitment options: 4-week paid contractor (recommended) or a 10–15 day intensive pilot for earlier signals.
- Compensation: prorated 4-week daily rate (market competitive) + clear conversion criteria.

Bootcamp weekly breakdown (example for inference team):
Week 0 (onboarding, pre-reads): access, local dev scaffold, meet core partners, set 2 measurable goals for the bootcamp.
Week 1 (diagnose & plan): triage the chosen ticket, run baseline experiments, and present a 1-page plan with metrics.
Week 2 (iterate & deliver): implement core changes, run engineering tests, performance benchmarks. Twice-weekly async updates + 1x 30m live sync.
Week 3 (polish & integrate): fix edge cases, add observability hooks, small canary rollout plan. Final demo to stakeholders and retrospective.

Bootcamp deliverables and success signals (examples):
- Working PR that meets the team’s merge criteria.
- Benchmark comparison showing measurable improvement (latency, cost, or error reduction).
- Clear rollout / rollback plan and test matrix.
- Positive feedback from at least 2 cross-functional partners (product, infra).

Post-bootcamp decision heuristics (manager + people ops):
- Recommend hire if: core deliverable merged or accepted by team, candidate demonstrates async/remote communication, and offers a clear 90-day plan with measurable impact items.
- Consider extended contract if substantial progress but not production-ready.

Manager onboarding checklist (on hire conversion):
- Access & infra: grant repo, CI, internal docs, monitoring dashboards within 48h.
- Assign mentor & buddy with weekly 1:1 cadence for first 6 weeks.
- Kickoff: set 30/60/90 deliverables aligned with bootcamp goals.
- Invite to relevant runbooks, pager rotations only after 30 days and explicit readiness.

People Ops runbook items (ops owner actions):
- Create paid-contract template and stipend payment workflow.
- Standardize async-kit artifacts and rubric sheet (team-level copy).
- Track time-to-hire and conversion rate for this experiment (separate metric in hiring dashboard).

Risks & mitigations:
- Bias toward candidates with spare time: mitigate by stipend and explicit time estimate.
- Intellectual property concerns: include IP consent clause for submitted artifacts.
- Manager capacity: require manager sign-off before offering bootcamp slot.

Open questions / discussion items (for people ops and hiring managers):
- What minimum paid stipend makes the funnel equitable across regions? (need finance input)
- Should certain senior levels skip the async lab and go straight to a condensed paid bootcamp?
- How do we standardize conversion compensation when moving from contractor to FT?

Appendix / Templates (links):
- Async assignment template (short README + skeleton repo)
- Rubric Google sheet (panel copy)
- Bootcamp weekly status template (standup + demo notes)

Notes to self (internal):
- Pilot this with two inference openings in Q4, cap at 6 bootcamp slots. Collect qualitative feedback from hiring managers and candidates.
- Iterate on stipend after first 20 candidates.
